roles.label: Administrator
roles.description: Approves any order in its tenant, including orders over 1000.

roles.label: Manager
roles.description: Approves orders up to 1000 in its tenant, not its own requests.

roles.label: Manager in tenant t2
roles.description: A manager in another tenant. Must not see or approve tenant t1 orders.

requirements.text: Signing in with a valid username and password returns a session token; a wrong password returns 401.
A request without a session token is refused with 401.
An order needs a non-blank item and a total greater than zero. A violation returns 422 and names the field.
An order total is a JSON number.
A user reads and approves only orders in its own tenant. Another tenant's order returns 404.
A manager approves a pending order up to 1000 in its own tenant, but not its own request.
An order over 1000 is approved only by an admin.
An order is approved once. A second approval returns 409.
A staff member cannot approve an order.
requirements.source: derived from the role descriptions in openapi.json; not stated as a rule

requirements.text: Export downloads the orders the user can see, as JSON.
requirements.source: the export control in the planted app; no spec

requirements.text: A failed approval is reported to the user as an error, and the approve control stays available.
Every form field has a visible label that names it.
requirements.source: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions

requirements.text: Touch targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels at phone widths.
requirements.source: WCAG 2.2 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced); the team has not chosen this level

requirements.text: The order table reflows at 320 CSS pixels with no clipped column.
A release build is not debuggable, allows no cleartext traffic, and declares no secret in its resources.
requirements.source: OWASP MASVS MSTG-RESILIENCE and MSTG-STORAGE checks for Android

permissions.noDeniedReason: the denial is the tenant condition, tested for each tenant in TC-ORD-03
every role may create orders in its own tenant

rules.condition: same tenant, not own request, total up to 1000

branches.summary: valid credentials open the orders page
a wrong password shows an error and no session is created
after an error the user can sign in again
a valid order is created and appears in the list
a blank item or a total of zero or less is rejected with the field named
a request without a session is refused
a manager approves an eligible pending order, and the status becomes approved
a second approval is a conflict, and an order over 1000 is refused for a manager
a staff member, or a manager on its own request, is refused

journeys.title: Read an order in another tenant

branches.summary: an order in the caller's tenant opens
an order in another tenant returns not found
a manager in another tenant cannot read tenant t1 orders
a successful approval shows the new status
a failed approval shows an error and keeps the control
the manager can retry the approval after the error
the export downloads the orders the user can see

journeys.title: Use the orders on a phone

branches.summary: the table and the approve control work at phone widths

journeys.title: Create an order with labelled fields

branches.summary: every field is announced with its label
an invalid field is described to the user
the release manifest is not debuggable and allows no cleartext
a debuggable manifest or a hardcoded key is reported

fixtures.description: Four orders: o-1 (staff, 500, t1), o-2 (staff, 5000, t1), o-3 (outsider, 100, t2), o-4 (manager, 300, t1). All pending. Reset by restarting the fixture server.
One account for each role, with credentials taken from the environment variables named on the role.

testCases.title: Sign-in returns a token for valid credentials
expected: 200 with a token and the user for valid credentials
401 for a wrong password

testCases.title: Requests without a token are refused
expected: 401 for a request without a token

testCases.title: Sign-in form shows a wrong-password error and opens the orders page
expected: a wrong password shows an error
a valid sign-in opens the orders page

testCases.title: Order creation validates the item and the total
expected: 422 naming item for a blank item
422 naming total for a total of zero or less
201 for a valid order

testCases.title: Order total is a number
expected: the total in the order detail is a JSON number

testCases.title: Another tenant's order is not readable
expected: 404 for an order in another tenant
200 for an order in the caller's tenant

testCases.title: A manager approves an eligible order and not its own
expected: 200 when a manager approves o-1 (500, owned by staff)
403 when a manager approves o-4 (its own request)

testCases.title: Orders over 1000 need an admin
expected: 403 when a manager approves o-2 (5000)
200 when an admin approves o-2

testCases.title: Concurrent approvals of one order: one succeeds
expected: two concurrent approvals of one order give one 200 and one 409
the approval count is 1 afterwards

testCases.title: A staff member cannot approve
expected: 403 when a staff member approves an order

testCases.title: The approval is stored
expected: the stored status is approved and the approval count is 1 after one approval

testCases.title: Export downloads the visible orders
expected: the export downloads orders.json with the visible orders

testCases.title: A failed approval shows an error and keeps the control
expected: a failed approval shows an error message
the approve control stays available after a failure

testCases.title: Form fields have visible labels
expected: each field has a visible label that names it

testCases.title: Approve control is large enough on a phone
expected: the approve control is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels at 390 pixels wide

testCases.title: The order table reflows on a narrow screen
expected: at 320 CSS pixels the order table reflows and no column is clipped

testCases.title: The create form shows the API's field error
expected: a blank item shows the field error returned by the API

testCases.title: The Android release manifest is not debuggable and allows no cleartext
expected: android:debuggable is false
android:usesCleartextTraffic is false
no hardcoded key in the resources

designMap.note: The fixture has no design files. Visual parity is not performed; spec checks only.
